Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexusGuard Technologies Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your telephone keypad if you would like to ask a question. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NexusGuard Technologies' results for the third quarter of 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Lisa Wong, Chief Security Officer; Tom Hargrove, VP of Sales; Emily Santos, Chief Marketing Officer; and Mike Thornton, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. NexusGuard Technologies delivered exceptional results in the third quarter, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. Our performance reflects the strength of our product portfolio, our expanding customer base, and our commitment to innovation. The adoption rate of Nexus One is accelerating, demonstrating the transformative impact on threat detection and response, and the unparalleled value we bring to our customers in unifying endpoint, network, cloud, and identity security.

Our strategic priorities are focused on eight key areas: accelerating platform adoption versus point products, driving performance in key product lines like cloud security and SASE, providing next quarter billings guidance, enhancing the effectiveness of our go-to-market strategy, achieving robust ARR growth quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year, increasing average deal sizes for new and existing customers, maintaining low churn rates with clear mitigation strategies, and managing the impact of currency fluctuations on revenue.

These priorities are not just goals—they're executing in real time, positioning us to capture share in a consolidating market where integrated platforms are dominating siloed solutions. Now, I'll turn the call over to Maria Chen to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Maria Chen: Thank you, Alex. We achieved record revenue of $450 million in the third quarter, representing a 45% increase year-over-year on a constant currency basis, or 40% as reported. Our gross margin remained strong at 80%, reflecting the scalability of our multi-tenant SaaS architecture, and we continued to invest aggressively in growth initiatives. Operating expenses were $320 million, up 35% year-over-year but in line with our plan to fuel R&D and sales expansion. Net income was $85 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.65, beating our guidance by 15%. We are increasing our full-year revenue guidance to $1.75 billion to $1.78 billion and earnings per share to $2.45 to $2.50, based on our strong performance to date and visibility into Q4.

Let me dive deeper into these metrics, starting with one of our most telling indicators: platform adoption rate versus point products. The cybersecurity landscape has shifted dramatically from siloed point solutions—like standalone EDR agents or legacy firewalls—to integrated platforms that deliver converged capabilities across endpoint, network, cloud, and identity security. This is our sweet spot with Nexus One, our cloud-native XDR and SASE powerhouse, which unifies CNAPP, CWPP, CSPM, and ZTNA into a single pane of glass with a shared telemetry lake.

In Q3, our platform business generated $285 million in ARR, up 52% year-over-year and 18% quarter-over-quarter. That's versus our point product portfolio—primarily legacy modules like standalone EPP and web gateway—which clocked in at $115 million in ARR, growing a respectable but decelerating 12% YoY. As a result, platforms now represent 71% of our total cybersecurity ARR, up from 58% a year ago and 65% last quarter. New ACV from platform deals averaged $1.2 million, 3.2 times higher than the $375,000 for point products. Our top 20 platform logos expanded 28% in net retention during the quarter, driven by land-and-expand dynamics as customers bolt on SASE and identity modules post-initial XDR deployment.

This isn't a blip—it's structural. Over the past 12 months, platform adoption has outpaced point products by 4x in net new bookings. We've seen our platform customer count swell to 2,450, a 41% YoY increase, while point-only customers have flatlined at around 1,200. This mirrors broader market dynamics: Gartner pegs the integrated platform market at $45 billion in 2024, growing 25% CAGR through 2028, while point solutions like discrete firewalls or email gateways are sub-10% growers amid consolidation fatigue. Post high-profile incidents like the Change Healthcare ransomware and Snowflake breaches, CISOs are ditching best-of-breed sprawl—averaging 45 tools per enterprise per our latest customer survey—for platforms that cut MTTR from days to minutes via AI-orchestrated response.

On the technical front, our Nexus Intelligence Fabric, a petabyte-scale data lake ingesting 10 trillion events daily across endpoints, networks, and clouds, powers GenAI-driven threat hunting, with features like Autonomous SOAR reducing alert fatigue by 85%—validated in our beta with Fortune 500 banks. We've rolled out Zero Trust Everywhere, integrating our SSPM with Okta and Ping Identity APIs for seamless identity orchestration. Nexus One's agentless CNAPP now covers 95% of AWS, Azure, and GCP workloads out-of-the-box, with auto-remediation for 70% of misconfigs. These give us sticky 135% NRR versus 105% for point customers.

Regionally, North America, 65% of revenue, hit 78% platform mix—led by hyperscalers like a major Big Tech firm expanding from $10M endpoint pilot to $50M full-stack SASE. EMEA, at 22% of revenue, reached 62% adoption, boosted by GDPR-driven compliance; we closed a landmark deal with a DAX 40 telco for converged 5G edge security. APAC, our 13% growth engine, lags at 51% platform penetration due to entrenched point vendors like Trend Micro and local data sovereignty hurdles in China and India. But Q3 APAC platform bookings surged 68% YoY on Singapore's Multi-Ministry ZTNA framework and Aussie critical infra regs. We're addressing this with FedRAMP High and IRAP certifications, plus sovereign cloud instances in Sydney and Tokyo.

Strategically, platform gross margins hit 82% in Q3, versus 74% for points. We've guided to $1.15 billion in RPO, with 65% weighted toward platforms. Q4 platform adoption should exceed 75%, fueled by our AWS Marketplace partnership—now 40% of wins originate there—and the pending acquisition of a boutique DSPM player. Customers tell us platforms deliver 40% TCO savings over point sprawl, with 3x faster threat coverage.

Next, on the performance of our key product lines, particularly cloud security and SASE, which together represented 62% of total revenue at $279 million, up 48% year-over-year. Cloud security delivered $178 million, a 42% YoY increase and 15% QoQ, with ARR at $785 million in a market IDC projects at 23% CAGR through 2028. Our CNAPP integrates CSPM, CWPP, and CIEM with proprietary ML for real-time anomaly detection, reducing false positives by 35%. We added 247 net new logos, bringing customers to 4,200 enterprises, ACV up 18% to $192,000, NRR at 122%. The GenAI security module contributed $22 million in new bookings post-OpenAI breaches.

North America at 58% of cloud security revenue, APAC up 67% YoY to $42 million via Alibaba and Tencent integrations, EMEA up 39% to $31 million on NIS2. We're launching adaptive micro-segmentation with eBPF ahead of competitors.

SASE hit $134 million, up 55% YoY and 21% sequentially, ARR $612 million, RPO up 62% to $950 million. It powers 3,800 customers, including 40% of Fortune 100, ACV up 22% to $168,000. Our single-vendor fabric delivers sub-50ms latency via 150+ PoPs, outperforming Cato in tests. SWG blocked 2.1 billion threats, up 41% YoY.

EMEA led SASE growth at 55% to $38 million on DORA, APAC 72% to $29 million, North America steady with federal CMMC deals. We're investing $150 million in capex for PoPs and GPU threat hunting, with DeepShield acquisition bolstering deception tech. Cross-sell attach at 68%, expecting 50%+ growth in FY2025.

Turning to ARR growth: Total ARR reached $478 million, up 14% QoQ from $419 million and 42% YoY from $336 million. Expansion revenue was 62% of the $59 million QoQ add, NRR at 128%. YoY fueled by 55% new ACV growth, multi-year deals at 68%. Aegis XDR 2.0 with GenAI drove 150 new logos. North America 68% of ARR, 16% QoQ/45% YoY; EMEA 15% QoQ; APAC 22% QoQ/68% YoY. Gross retention 95%, guiding Q3 QoQ 13-15%, FY24 YoY 40-42%.

Average deal size: New logo ACV $185,000, up 23% YoY/8% QoQ, driven by CyberShield One bundling XDR, NDR, CWPP. North America $210,000, EMEA $165,000 up 35%, APAC $140,000 up 45%. Existing ACV $320,000, up 18% YoY, NRR 128%, upsells via GSPM (42%), SecureMesh ZTNA (55%). 65% multi-product deals, AWS 22% of new ACV. Q4 new $195-200k, existing $330k+.

Churn: Gross dollar churn 6.8% annualized, down from 7.7% QoQ/8.5% YoY; logo churn 4.2%. Outperforms peers at 8-10%. Drivers: economic 42%, competitive 28% (Palo Alto, Microsoft), product gaps 18%, M&A 9%, other 3%. North America 5.9%, EMEA 8.1%, APAC 7.4%. Dollar expansion offset 115% of churn. Initiatives: ShieldAI Retain predicts churn 45 days out (87% accuracy, recovered $4.2M), Kubernetes analytics, SASE 41% penetration, MDR bundling. Guide FY24 6.5%, NRR 125-130%.

Currency impact: 55% international revenue, Q3 constant currency +28% vs. reported +22%, $42M headwind (3.3 pts). USD up 8% vs. EUR, 12% GBP, 6% JPY. Americas $576M +32%, EMEA $384M +14% local +25%, APAC $256M +18% local +24%. Hedging 70% exposure, dynamic pricing 40% EMEA, APAC to 20% ARR. Q4 2-3% headwind, constant 27-30%.

Next quarter billings guidance: $335-345 million, midpoint $340M +28% YoY/12% QoQ. New ACV 40%, DBNR 128%, RPO $2.8B +42% YoY. Americas 58%, EMEA 27%, APAC 15% +18% seq. Investments in AI hardening, ServiceNow/Snowflake partnerships, M&A.

We're raising full-year guidance accordingly.

Dr. Raj Patel: Thank you, Maria. Our technology team is focused on developing cutting-edge security solutions that leverage the latest advancements in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and cloud computing. Key areas include advancing our Nexus Intelligence Fabric for GenAI threat hunting, agentless CNAPP coverage across major clouds, and Zero Trust Everywhere with SSPM integrations, all driving the platform flywheel we discussed.

Lisa Wong: Security remains our top priority. We are continuously monitoring the threat landscape—ransomware up 37%, API vulnerabilities surging 300%—and adapting our security posture to protect customers and infrastructure, with autonomous SOAR and post-quantum primitives countering emerging risks.

Tom Hargrove: We are seeing strong demand across geographies and verticals. Our sales team is building relationships and expanding share, with channel partners at 68% of bookings, AWS Marketplace up 150% QoQ, and freemium conversions at 22% lowering CAC to $18,000.

Emily Santos: Our marketing efforts focus on brand awareness and demand gen via digital, PR, events, and thought leadership, positioning NexusGuard as a trusted advisor amid zero-trust shifts and regulatory waves like NIS2 and CMMC.

Mike Thornton: Our product strategy delivers innovative, integrated solutions addressing evolving needs. We're gathering feedback to exceed expectations, with upcoming launches like adaptive micro-segmentation and Quantum Shield ensuring we stay ahead.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for the Q&A session. First question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs.

David Lee: Great quarter, congrats. Can you expand on platform adoption trends versus points, especially regionally and what drives the NRR differential?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, David. As Maria detailed, platforms are 71% of ARR, up sharply, with 4x outpacing points in bookings. North America at 78% mix, EMEA 62%, APAC accelerating to 51% with regs. The 135% NRR vs. 105% comes from native capabilities like our data lake and auto-remediation, creating stickiness customers can't replicate with points.

Operator: Next question comes from Priya Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Priya Patel: On guidance, how does next quarter billings reflect product line momentum, and any macro risks?

Maria Chen: Priya, the $335-345M embeds cloud and SASE strength, new ACV at 40%, expansions via 128% DBNR. Risks like sales cycles in SMBs and forex are factored, but RPO growth and partnerships mitigate—we're confident.

Operator: Next question comes from Chris Wong with JPMorgan.

Chris Wong: Thoughts on ARR growth sustainability, especially APAC and innovation catalysts?

Dr. Raj Patel: Chris, 14% QoQ/42% YoY is durable, APAC at 22%/68% on sovereign clouds. Catalysts like XDR 2.0 GenAI, Quantum Shield, and Snowflake DSPM integrations position us for 40%+ FY24.

Operator: Next question comes from Laura Kim with Barclays.

Laura Kim: Churn details—economic pressures seem sticky; how are you addressing competitive displacement?

Lisa Wong: Laura, economic at 42% but down YoY with flexible pricing. Competitive 28%, countered by ShieldAI Retain recovering ARR and Kubernetes/Splunk fixes. Multi-product at 72% raises switching costs—NRR holds strong.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your insightful questions. We are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you to our employees, customers, and partners.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
